title: Dual-Core Multi-Chip Module (MCM) Integration vs. Single-Core Die
where_in_paper: Processor Chip and MCM Architecture / Executive Summary
decision: Integrate two full 64-bit symmetric processing cores onto a single silicon die and package four such dies on a multi-chip module (MCM) to form an 8-way SMP building block.
alternatives_or_rejected: Building traditional single-core processor dies interconnected at the board level.
rationale: Placing two cores on the same die drastically reduces inter-processor communication latency, enables extremely high-bandwidth L2/L3 cache sharing, and reduces package footprint while providing high instruction throughput per package.
outcome: Achieved a dense 8-way SMP MCM module with high-bandwidth chip-to-chip and module-to-module interconnects, forming the core building block for large SMP systems.
weakest_point: Exact page number for the MCM layout section

title: Instruction Grouping and Execution (I-Group / Slice Architecture)
where_in_paper: Instruction Execution Pipeline / Dispatch and Completion
decision: Form fixed groups of up to five instructions (I-groups) at dispatch that travel together through the pipeline and complete atomically in program order.
alternatives_or_rejected: Fully independent, instruction-by-instruction out-of-order dispatch and completion tracking.
rationale: Group-based tracking significantly reduces the hardware complexity and queue tracking overhead of tracking dozens of individual out-of-order instructions through completion.
outcome: Simplified completion logic and tracking queues while sustaining up to 5-instruction dispatch/completion width per cycle.
weakest_point: Exact max count of instructions in an I-group across all execution paths

title: On-Chip Shared L2 Cache Design
decision: Implement a large, unified L2 cache shared directly by both processor cores on the same chip, organized into multiple autonomous modules/slices.
alternatives_or_rejected: Dedicated private L2 caches for each core on the die.
rationale: A shared L2 dynamically adapts to asymmetric workloads between the two cores, reduces overall L2 cache miss rates, and eliminates duplicate cache entries for shared data/instructions.
outcome: Provided high-bandwidth, low-latency cache access for both cores with efficient hardware cache coherence mechanisms.
weakest_point: Specific latency numbers or cycle count figures given for L2 cache access

title: Distributed Point-to-Point Interconnect and Coherence Protocol
decision: Use point-to-point buses with distributed snoop logic across MCM packages rather than a single global shared command bus.
alternatives_or_rejected: Centralized global bus interconnect architecture for multi-module SMP scaling.
rationale: Centralized buses create severe pin count, bandwidth, and electrical physical scaling bottlenecks at gigahertz clock speeds.
outcome: Allowed scalable high-bandwidth interconnect across 32-core (4 MCM) SMP configurations.
weakest_point: Specific terminology used for the snoop bus protocol layers

title: Hardware Instruction Prefetching and Dynamic Data Prefetch Engines
decision: Implement aggressive hardware-based stream prefetch engines to fetch data and instructions into L2/L3 caches ahead of execution.
alternatives_or_rejected: Relying purely on software/compiler-directed prefetch instructions.
rationale: Hardware stream detection captures dynamic memory access patterns and stride changes in real-time without increasing instruction stream bandwidth overhead.
outcome: Significantly mitigated long memory latency stalls for scientific and commercial database workloads.
weakest_point: Number of concurrent stream prefetch engines supported per core
